reuse.why: Introduces a shared skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate in shared/schedules.ts and routes getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template through it, reusing getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag rather than adding new ones.

duplication.why: Dropping weekend occurrences is implemented twice: getNextWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts and an over-fetch-and-filter chain in getUpcomingDates.

placement.why: The predicate and the next-weekday search live in shared/schedules.ts next to getNextDate and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the getUpcomingDates variant stays local in schedules/app.ts.

scope.why: Only the schedule date paths affected by the rule, the frequency now carried in parseRecurDate's data, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: The 'does this schedule skip' question has one answer, but the skip itself is done two different ways and schedule-template passes an inverted noSkipWeekend computed from the predicate while keeping its own skipWeekend ? move ternary, which is hard to reason about.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All three sites call skipsWeekendOccurrences; getUpcomingDates does not use getNextDate, but it did not before either.

disguised_duplication.where: The weekday-only selection appears as getNextWeekdayOccurrence (take N, find non-weekend) in shared/schedules.ts and as take(count * 7).filter(!isWeekend).slice in getUpcomingDates in schedules/app.ts.

one_place.where: Whether the rule applies is decided once by skipsWeekendOccurrences, but what it does (drop weekend occurrences instead of moving them) is applied separately in getNextDate, in getUpcomingDates, and indirectly in schedule-template via an inverted noSkipWeekend argument plus its own skipWeekend ternary.
